adminData.integrity.title: Data integrity
adminData.integrity.desc: Checks that compare what a record stores against the records behind it. Every finding names the check that produced it, so you can tell a real problem from a rule that has gone stale.
adminData.integrity.runSummary: Run {run} read {records} records across {checks} checks and found {findings}.
adminData.integrity.runSummary.clean: Every check passed. Run {run} read {records} records across {checks} checks.

adminData.integrity.clear.heading: Every check passed
adminData.integrity.clear.body: {records} records were read and none of them disagreed with the records behind it.

integrity.check.ref.trip-links.title: Trips point at records that exist
integrity.check.ref.trip-links.desc: Every trip names a rider, a captain and a subscription. This check opens each of those ids and reports the ones that resolve to nothing.
integrity.check.ref.subscription-links.t: Subscriptions point at records that exist
integrity.check.ref.subscription-links.d: Every subscription names the rider who holds it and the captain who serves it. This check reports the ones whose ids resolve to nothing.
integrity.check.ref.person-links.title: Rider and captain link lists resolve
integrity.check.ref.person-links.desc: A rider record lists its subscriptions, its trips and its corporate account; a captain lists its trips. This check opens every id in those lists.
integrity.check.ref.ticket-subject.title: Tickets point at a customer who exists
integrity.check.ref.ticket-subject.desc: A ticket names a rider, a captain or a corporate account. This check looks the id up in the collection the ticket says it belongs to.
integrity.check.ref.money-party.title: Money records name a party that exists
integrity.check.ref.money-party.desc: Payouts, escrow holds and deductions each name a captain, and some name a rider, a subscription or a trip. This check opens all of them.
integrity.check.ref.ledger-subject.title: Ledger postings name a subject and an entry that exist
integrity.check.ref.ledger-subject.desc: A posting on a party account carries the id of that party, and belongs to a journal entry. This check opens both, and the posting a reversal says it reverses.
integrity.check.agree.party-name.title: Two records agree on a person’s name
integrity.check.agree.party-name.desc: Trips, subscriptions, tickets, payouts, holds and deductions each carry a copy of a person’s name so a table can render without a second read. This check compares every copy against the record that owns the name.
integrity.check.agree.escrow-amount.titl: A subscription and its escrow hold agree
integrity.check.agree.escrow-amount.desc: A subscription shows the escrow held against it; Financials holds the record of that escrow. This check compares the two amounts and reports a subscription still showing escrow that has been released.
integrity.check.agree.aggregate-vs-recor: A lifetime total has records behind it

A rider or captain whose stored trip total is larger than the trips on file is expected — this console keeps a recent window and billing keeps the lifetime. One whose stored total has nothing at all behind it is not, and that is what this check reports.
A status agrees with the fields that justify it
A subscriber holds a subscription, a late trip carries its lateness, a suspended captain carries a reason, a cancelled subscription carries the moment it was cancelled. This check reads each pair.
integrity.check.invariant.counters.title: Counters on one record add up
integrity.check.invariant.counters.desc: Open subscription slots follow from the cap minus the active ones; completed trips cannot exceed the trips a plan includes. This check does the arithmetic.
integrity.check.money.trip-split.title: A fare splits exactly
integrity.check.money.trip-split.desc: The fare, the captain’s earnings, the extra-stop fee and the Eyvar cut are one identity. Money is whole halalas, so any remainder at all means one of the four was computed somewhere else.
integrity.check.money.wallet-balance.tit: A wallet balance matches its ledger
integrity.check.money.wallet-balance.des: The balance on a rider record and the closing balance of that rider’s wallet ledger are meant to be the same number from the same source. This check reads both.
integrity.check.money.journal-balance.de: Debits equal credits on every entry, and both equal the total the entry states. An entry that does not balance is refused rather than written, so anything found here was written before that rule existed.
integrity.check.money.payout-net.title: A payout’s net follows from the ledger
integrity.check.money.payout-net.desc: A deduction marked applied has moved money on the captain’s payable, and a payout still marked due does not owe a negative amount. This check reads the ledger for both.

integrity.detail.overCapacity: Holds {active} subscriptions against a cap of {max}.
integrity.detail.tripsOverIncluded: Records {completed} trips against the {included} the plan includes.
integrity.detail.tripsOverRequired: Records {completed} trips against the {required} the hold requires.
integrity.detail.fareSplitDisagrees: Fare {fareHalalas} less earnings {earningsHalalas} less extras {extrasHalalas} leaves {deltaHalalas} unaccounted for beside a stated cut of {cutHalalas}.
integrity.detail.walletDisagrees: Stores a balance of {recordHalalas}. Its ledger closes at {ledgerHalalas}, a difference of {deltaHalalas}.
integrity.detail.entryTotalDisagrees: States a total of {statedHalalas} against lines summing to {linesHalalas}.
integrity.detail.deductionNotPosted: Is marked applied and moved nothing: no posting on {captainId} names it, so the payable is {amountHalalas} too high.
integrity.detail.negativeNet: Is due {payableHalalas} against a cash debt of {cashDebtHalalas}, which nets to {netHalalas}.

onboarding.title: Getting started
onboarding.intro.owner: You're accountable for the whole console — policy, people, money, and the decisions nobody else can make.
onboarding.intro.opsManager: You keep trips covered and captains working — applications, requests, assurance and dispatch.
onboarding.intro.finance: You move money and account for it — payouts, escrow, deductions and reconciliation. You can see profiles, and you cannot change a captain's status.
onboarding.intro.support: You answer riders and captains, and you're the first person to hear when something goes wrong. You can see a safety incident and you cannot decide one — an Ops Manager does.

onboarding.step.common.account.title: Check the account that is now yours
onboarding.step.common.account.body: Confirm the number your codes go to, then review your active sessions and end anything you don't recognise.
onboarding.step.common.mywork.title: Claim one item, then release it
onboarding.step.common.mywork.body: Operations › My Work is where every queue reaches you. Claim something from Unassigned and release it again, so you learn what a claim is before you're holding six.
onboarding.step.common.audit.title: Find your own name in the activity log
onboarding.step.common.audit.body: Everything you do here is recorded with your name on it. Read the log once, and read who is on call, so you know who to reach at 2am.
onboarding.step.owner.team.title: Read the role matrix, and decide if it still holds
onboarding.step.owner.team.body: One account holds manage_settings, and that key gates 39 of the console's 131 permission checks. Decide whether that is still acceptable.
onboarding.step.owner.policy.title: Read the policy you are accountable for
onboarding.step.owner.policy.body: Dispatch radius, operating limits, SLA targets and reason codes. Read them once, deliberately, rather than the first time one is disputed.
onboarding.step.owner.position.title: State the current contribution margin
onboarding.step.owner.position.body: The trial balance and the contribution margin are the two numbers you'll be asked about. This is where they live, and this step is done when you can say them out loud.
onboarding.step.owner.pricing.title: Settle how captains are paid
onboarding.step.owner.pricing.body: The console computes captain earnings four different ways and nobody has chosen one. That decision is outstanding, and it is yours.
onboarding.step.finance.ledger.title: Read a ledger before you post to one
onboarding.step.finance.ledger.body: Learn the sign convention, and learn that a posted row is never edited — it is reversed by a second row. Nothing in Financials undoes itself.
onboarding.step.finance.escrow.title: Read what releasing escrow does, without releasing it
onboarding.step.finance.escrow.body: Open one escrow row and read it through. Release moves money to a captain, and there is no undo — only a reversing entry.
onboarding.step.finance.reconciliation.t: Work one reconciliation item end to end
onboarding.step.finance.reconciliation.b: Claim it, decide it, and watch the row convert in place. This queue is how cash and captain debt stay true to each other.
onboarding.step.finance.goodwill.title: Find the cap that bounds a goodwill credit
onboarding.step.finance.goodwill.body: You and Support share one compensation cap. Find the number before a rider asks you to go past it.
onboarding.step.finance.routing.title: Know which queue reaches you
onboarding.step.finance.routing.body: Disputes route to Finance. Turn role routing off once in My Work and see what changes, so you know what you're filtering out.
onboarding.step.ops.application.title: Decide one captain application end to end
onboarding.step.ops.application.body: Read the documents, then approve or reject. The row gives you a tick, a cross and View — there is no menu to open.
onboarding.step.ops.requests.title: Claim, work and dispose of one request
onboarding.step.ops.requests.body: Watch the SLA clock while you hold it. Read what a breach means — a breach is a missed target, not a failure to act.
onboarding.step.ops.assurance.title: Cover one trip before it departs
onboarding.step.ops.assurance.body: Trip Assurance lists subscriptions with no backup captain. Register or replace a captain on one of them.
onboarding.step.ops.dispatch.title: Tell a stale feed from a dead one
onboarding.step.ops.dispatch.body: Live Dispatch shows a freshness line. Learn the difference between data that is late and data that has stopped, before you act on either.
onboarding.step.ops.fairness.title: Read one suspension appeal from the captain's side
onboarding.step.ops.fairness.body: Captain Fairness shows you the economics a suspension takes away. Read one before you're asked to answer for a decision.
onboarding.step.support.ticket.title: Answer one ticket end to end
onboarding.step.support.ticket.body: Open it, respond, and resolve it with a reason code. The reason code is what makes a ticket countable later.
onboarding.step.support.profile.title: Open a 360° profile, and know what you may not do with it
onboarding.step.support.profile.body: One profile carries every piece of personal data the console holds about a person, across 11 record types. Open it only when the work in front of you needs it.
onboarding.step.support.goodwill.title: Credit a rider, inside your cap
onboarding.step.support.goodwill.body: This is the one money action you take mid-call, and it's bounded by policy. Find the cap before you need it.
onboarding.step.support.boundary.title: Know what you may not decide, and who does
onboarding.step.support.boundary.body: You can see every safety incident and you cannot decide one — an Ops Manager does. Read one incident, and stop there.
